extracted.intended_audience: UK companies, corporate tax managers, in-house counsel and patent owners considering a Patent Box claim
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on qualifying for and calculating the UK Patent Box reduced corporation tax rate (10%) on profits attributable to patented technology, including eligibility, required activities, calculation stages, timeline and practical tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced corporation tax rate (10%) on patent profits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Box tax incentive is a reduced corporation tax rate of 10% on net profits attributed to patents (after certain deductions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aims to encourage development of patentable technology in the UK and compares favourably with the main corporation tax rate (25%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of revenue and qualifying patents
rubrics_metrics.description: All revenue from a UK company can count towards your Patent Box application and any patent in a qualifying patent office can count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UK national patents attract low official fees, so are a cheap way to qualify for the Patent Box without the need to file in other countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification by legal ownership or exclusive licence
rubrics_metrics.description: You may qualify for Patent Box through legal ownership of the patent and/or exclusive license from the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents acquired from or developed in collaboration with other companies may also qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying patent jurisdictions (EEA/UK/European, not US)
rubrics_metrics.description: It can be a UK or European patent, or a patent granted by another EEA country with similar patentability criteria, such as a German patent. US patents do not qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: US patents may cover subject-matter (e.g. business methods) that would not be patentable in the UK, so are excluded from qualifying patent offices for this purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territoriality of profit source
rubrics_metrics.description: The tax incentive is not limited to profits derived from countries where the patent is granted; instead, the existence of a qualifying patent is taken as an indication that the technology meets the requirements of technicality, novelty and inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profits earned anywhere can be considered provided there is a qualifying patent covering the relevant technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant requirement and retrospective qualifying profits
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending patent applications do not qualify, but once a patent is granted, profits arising up to 6 years before grant may qualify for the reduced tax rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing of grant affects eligibility for prior-year profits; plan filing/grant strategy accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying development requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The company must have undertaken 'qualifying development', by making a significant contribution to the creation or development of the invention claimed in the patent, or a product incorporating the patented invention; mere ownership of the patent is not enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A company can also qualify if it actively manages the portfolio of patent rights for another company in the same group that has undertaken the 'qualifying development'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 — Identifying qualifying patents / relevant IP income
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying qualifying patents or patent rights ('relevant IP income') means calculating the basic profit attributed to qualifying income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the initial step to determine which patents and which revenue streams will be treated as patent-derived for Patent Box purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 — Calculating qualifying residual profit
rubrics_metrics.description: You can calculate the qualifying residual profit by deducting routine profit the Treasury expects that you would have made without benefitting from patented technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Treasury assumes a routine return of 10% on expenses; use this assumption when determining the portion of profit attributable to routine (non-innovative) activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 3 — Removing marketing assets return
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing assets return refers to any profits attributed to brands and marketing that do not depend on innovation. Once these are removed you pro-rate patent and non-patent profit to give the patent box benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate returns attributable to branding/marketing from those attributable to patented innovation, then apportion profits before applying the 10% rate to patent-derived profit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Box timeline (key filing and grant milestones)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical timeline milestones relevant to Patent Box planning: 0 months filing/priority date (e.g. UK application); 12 months file PCT/national application claiming priority; 18 months publication date; (30–31 months enter PCT national phase — optional); 3–4.5 years grant of UK and other national applications (earlier if the Green Channel applies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these milestones to plan filings and to understand when granted patents may allow retrospective profit claims (subject to the 6-year rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic filing and enforcement considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents may be filed purely to gain a tax benefit: there is no need to enforce the patents against competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before applying, check whether existing products already contain qualifying patents or employ qualifying patents in their production. Consider whether patented ideas could legitimately be included to enhance production processes or product functionality when developing new products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for specialist tax advice
rubrics_metrics.description: The tax implications of the Patent Box are complex, and specialist tax advice will be needed to determine the proportion of profits that qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage specialist tax advisers (and patent advisers) to calculate qualifying income, residual profit, marketing asset adjustments and to prepare a compliant claim.
